description: Fix the two actual AppMarket rejection causes in the manifest and the packaging: rewrite src/main/resources/appian-plugin.xml to the Appian 26.9 shape (key de.hock.mqtt, real vendor, application-version min 26.9.0.0, new de.hock.mqtt.* class FQNs), and change the maven-assembly descriptor so the single shipped jar contains its own .java sources beside the .class files, carries Paho under META-INF/lib instead of root lib/, ships a third-party notice, and is the only jar in target/. Depends on FEAT-001 for the new class FQNs. Implements items 6-10b and the packaging half of item 14 of .agents/tasks/appmarket-compliance-plan.md.
steps: Rewrite src/main/resources/appian-plugin.xml (the REAL manifest - do not confuse it with the identically named assembly descriptor): set key="de.hock.mqtt" on <appian-plugin> (it must not start with com.appian); keep name="MQTT Broker Connected System"; in <plugin-info> keep the existing real <description>, replace <vendor name="Appian" url="https://www.appian.com"/> with <vendor name="Hock" url="https://hock.de"/> (claiming Appian as vendor is itself a rejection risk; the URL is a placeholder - record in findings that the user must supply the real one), keep <version>1.0.0.0</version>, and change <application-version min="18.4.0.0"/> to min="26.9.0.0".

In the same file update all three class= attributes to de.hock.mqtt.template.MqttConnectedSystemTemplate, de.hock.mqtt.integration.MqttPublishIntegration, de.hock.mqtt.integration.MqttSubscribeIntegration. Keep every key= and name= attribute on <connected-system-template> and both nested <integration-template> elements EXACTLY as they are (MqttConnectedSystemTemplate, MqttPublishIntegration, MqttSubscribeIntegration) - they must stay equal to the @TemplateId names, and changing a @TemplateId would break already-deployed connected systems for no compliance gain. There is no <client-api> element in this plug-in. Also refresh the file's header comment, which names the old FQNs.

Verify the i18n bundle against the real simple class names: src/main/resources/resources_en_US.properties must contain MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.name/.description, MqttPublishIntegration.name/.description, and MqttSubscribeIntegration.name/.description, case sensitive. All six are present and correct today and the rename does not change them - confirm rather than edit, and only add or fix a key if one is genuinely missing or miscased.

Rename src/assembly/appian-plugin.xml to src/assembly/plugin-assembly.xml (it IS an assembly descriptor, ASSEMBLY/2.1.0 namespace, not a plug-in manifest; the duplicate filename is a maintenance trap in exactly the file this task changes) and update the pom's maven-assembly-plugin <descriptor> to src/assembly/plugin-assembly.xml.

In src/assembly/plugin-assembly.xml add a second <fileSet> inside the existing <fileSets>, after the ${project.build.outputDirectory} one, so sources ship root-mirrored next to their classes: <fileSet><directory>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</directory><outputDirectory>/</outputDirectory><includes><include>**/*.java</include></includes></fileSet>. Add a comment naming the AppMarket policy and noting that only src/main/java is included so test sources stay out. DO NOT add maven-source-plugin - a sibling -sources.jar does not satisfy 'source within the executable' - and DO NOT add a <build><resources> block, which would put .java on the test classpath and risks silently dropping the manifest by overriding the default resource root.

In the same descriptor change the dependencySet <outputDirectory> from lib to META-INF/lib. Appian's plug-in classloader resolves nested jars from META-INF/lib/, so Paho at root lib/ would very likely fail to resolve at runtime, and Paho classes are referenced directly by PahoMqttClientAdapter, ConnectOptionsFactory, and both integrations. Keep <useProjectArtifact>false</useProjectArtifact> and <scope>runtime</scope> so the provided-scope connected-systems-core stays excluded. This project BUNDLES Paho as a nested jar and does not shade it - keep it that way; shading would rewrite package names and make the shipped sources disagree with the shipped classes.

Create THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md at the repo root naming the one bundled third-party library: org.eclipse.paho:org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3:1.2.5, dual-licensed EPL-2.0 / EDL-1.0, with EDL-1.0 (permissive, BSD-3-clause style) as the license relied upon for redistribution. State that no copyleft library is bundled and that connected-systems-core is provided scope and never shipped. Ship it at the jar root with a third <fileSet>: <directory>${project.basedir}</directory><outputDirectory>/</outputDirectory><includes><include>THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md</include></includes>.

Make exactly one artifact land in target/: in pom.xml add a maven-jar-plugin block pinned to version 3.4.1 whose only execution overrides the implicit one with <id>default-jar</id><phase>none</phase>, and add <archive><addMavenDescriptor>false</addMavenDescriptor></archive> to the maven-assembly-plugin <configuration> so the shipped jar carries no META-INF/maven/**. Today both jars carry appian-plugin.xml at their root and an operator could deploy the wrong one. FALLBACK, only if mvn clean package then fails because the project artifact file is null: revert the phase-none override, keep default-jar, and instead configure maven-jar-plugin with <excludes><exclude>appian-plugin.xml</exclude></excludes> plus <addMavenDescriptor>false</addMavenDescriptor> so the plain jar no longer looks deployable. Record in findings which path you ended on and why.

Run the full archive verification and record the actual numbers in findings: 33 .java entries all under de/hock/mqtt/, 48 .class entries, appian-plugin.xml at the archive root with no directory prefix, resources_en_US.properties at the root, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md at the root, META-INF/lib/org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3-1.2.5.jar present, zero ^lib/ entries, zero ProjectStructureTest entries, zero com/appian/mqtt paths, zero META-INF/maven entries, and connected-systems-core absent.
